title: 17 Aug 2026 (Riyadh)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Riyadh, 17 August 2026

questions.question: During parotid surgery, how is the facial nerve identified?
questions.exp: The main trunk of the facial nerve exits the stylomastoid foramen and is found using landmarks such as the mastoid process and tragal pointer.
questions.b: Near the mastoid process, as it leaves the stylomastoid foramen
questions.d: At the angle of the mandible

questions.question: A 4-month-old weighed 3.5 kg at birth. Head circumference was 35 cm at birth and is now 47 cm; length went from 50 to 60 cm. There is no change in suckling. What will you do to diagnose the cause?
questions.exp: Rapid head growth needs imaging; in a well infant with an open fontanelle, ultrasound is first.

questions.question: A toddler has breath-holding attacks. What is the management?
A child has Guillain-Barré syndrome. What is the treatment?
A child has recurrent bitemporal headaches. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bilateral (bitemporal) headache is common in childhood migraine.

questions.question: An infant has infantile spasms. What is the treatment when tuberous sclerosis is the cause?
A newborn has a scalp swelling that crosses the midline. What is it?
questions.exp: Caput crosses sutures; cephalhaematoma does not.

questions.question: A 2-month-old has Hb 9 g/dL with normal indices and is otherwise well. What do you do?
questions.exp: The Hb nadir of about 9-11 g/dL at 8-12 weeks is physiological. The recall writer chose oral iron.

questions.question: A boy with head trauma has irregular breathing, bradycardia and high blood pressure. What do you do first?
questions.exp: Cushing triad means impending herniation: secure the airway, then reduce ICP.
questions.c: Intubate and ventilate, then give mannitol or hypertonic saline

questions.question: A baby rolled off the bed and immediately had impaired consciousness. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Immediate deterioration suggests subdural haemorrhage; consider abuse in an infant.

questions.question: A child fell down the stairs without loss of consciousness, had good vital signs, and hours later became drowsy. What is the cause?
A child with seizures had 2 doses of lorazepam in the ambulance. What do you give now?
A picture shows a brain abscess. What is the treatment?
A 10-month-old with otitis media on amoxicillin for 5 days becomes irritable. What do you do?
A child has lower limb hypotonia, reduced reflexes and a positive Babinski sign. What is the diagnosis?
A child on steroids for nephrotic syndrome has severe bilateral flank pain, WBC 22 with neutrophilia, urine WBC 2 and RBC 1500. What is the best investigation?
A 12-year-old girl has dark urine, abdominal pain, high BP, fever 39, protein ++, RBC >10 and WBC >10. What is the diagnosis?
A 7-year-old boy has nocturnal enuresis only, no social problems and is well in the day. What is the cause?
A baby on constipation drugs has haematuria and pyuria. Which test assesses the kidneys?
Which investigations look for kidney abnormalities after a UTI?
questions.exp: US for anatomy, DMSA for scarring, MCUG for reflux.

questions.question: What causes arthritis (septic) in sickle cell disease most often?
Thrombocytopenia with small platelets suggests which disease?
A child has bruises, giant platelets and thrombocytopenia. What is the diagnosis?
A haemophilia patient took factor VIII but did not improve. What is next?
Which is vitamin K dependent?
A child had URTI 2 weeks ago and now has bruises on the chin and elsewhere, platelets 25,000, and new bruises appear over old ones. What is the diagnosis?
In bronchiolitis, what is an indication for hospital admission?
questions.exp: Hypoxia or cyanosis, apnoea, poor feeding.

questions.question: LVH occurs in all of the following EXCEPT which?
questions.exp: In TGA the RV is systemic, so RVH is seen.

questions.question: What ECG finding after surgical correction of TGA is typical?
A child with VSD is on furosemide. What do you add next?
questions.exp: Afterload reduction with an ACE inhibitor (or digoxin).

questions.question: A 12-year-old boy, length 115 cm, has a systolic murmur and weak pulses. What is the lesion?
A child has congested neck veins, muffled heart sounds, hypotension and tachycardia. What type of shock?
A newborn is drooling, the abdomen is soft and he passed meconium. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Drooling with gas in the bowel suggests OA with distal TEF.

questions.question: A 3-week-old breastfed baby has jaundice with yellow stools and raised ALP. The mother fears bile duct obstruction. What is the first test?
questions.exp: Measure conjugated bilirubin first; if raised, investigate cholestasis.

questions.question: A 1-year-old had Hirschsprung repair at 2 days and now has fever, pain and distension. What do you do?
A child has grossly bloody maroon stools. Which explains the anaemia?
A picture shows a membrane-covered abdominal wall defect at the umbilicus. What is it?
X-ray shows a coiled NG tube. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Coiled tube in the upper pouch.

questions.question: A 4.5-year-old has staccato speech (stuttering) with normal development. What do you do?
questions.exp: Developmental stuttering often resolves; refer if persisting beyond 6 months or distressing.
questions.d: Re-evaluate later, or speech therapy if persistent

questions.question: A 13-year-old has severe abdominal pain and difficulty swallowing for 6 months; repeated visits found no abnormalities. What is the diagnosis?
A girl says her brother wants to hit her; he says mother loves the girl more. What is the advice?
A girl has disorganised speech, visual and auditory hallucinations and a father with the same illness. What is the diagnosis?
A child with a single central incisor and cleft palate (midline defect) has which hormone deficiency most commonly?
questions.exp: Midline defects associate with GH deficiency.

questions.question: Which condition causes undervirilisation (ambiguous genitalia) in a 46,XY male?
questions.exp: 5α-reductase deficiency (and 3β-HSD or 17-OH deficiency in CAH) cause undervirilised males; 21-OH deficiency virilises females.

questions.question: In which salivary gland are stones most common?
questions.exp: Submandibular secretions are thick and flow upward.

questions.question: A neonate has cleft lip and palate, a heart murmur and failure to thrive. Which associated problem should be looked for?
questions.exp: Midline clefts associate with pituitary hormone deficiency; also consider 22q11 deletion.

questions.question: A 2-month-old has persistent vomiting, abnormal genitalia, recurrent dehydration, Na 127 and K 6. What is the diagnosis?
A term newborn has cyanosis and apnoea worse when feeding and better when crying. What is the quickest diagnostic step?
questions.exp: Bilateral choanal atresia; confirm with CT nose.
questions.a: Pass a catheter through the nose

questions.question: An infant has no head lag and smiles. What is the age?
questions.exp: No head lag by about 4 months.

questions.question: A 12-year-old girl's height velocity chart shows growth stopped at 10 years; menarche was at 10.5 years and examination is normal. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Early puberty causes early epiphyseal fusion and growth arrest.

questions.question: A 7-day-old has rising jaundice, WBC 19,000 and raised AST and ALT. What is the cause?
A girl looks normal except for a webbed neck and short stature. What is the investigation?
A child with otitis media and a bulging drum finished 10 days of antibiotics and is well. What do you do?
A newborn has a mass protruding from the nose. What do you do?
What is the normal A-a oxygen gradient?
questions.exp: Normal is under 10-15 mmHg in children.

questions.question: An infant has recurrent epistaxis and uses local steroid spray. What is the likely cause?
A child with epiglottitis is drooling with O2 saturation 97%. What do you do?
questions.c: Secure the airway by nasotracheal intubation in theatre

questions.question: A child snores at night. What is the investigation?
Where is an aspirated peanut most likely located?
A child has a ranula. What is the best treatment?
questions.exp: Excision of the sublingual gland prevents recurrence.

questions.question: A child has abdominal pain with fever and cough. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: Lower-lobe pneumonia can present with abdominal pain.

questions.question: A child with a scorpion sting is assessed. Which finding is expected?
questions.exp: Scorpion venom causes autonomic storm: tachycardia, hypertension, sweating, hypersalivation and priapism. Bradycardia can occur early from cholinergic effects; the recall writer was unsure.

questions.question: A child took a large dose of an oral decongestant and has irritability and HR 200. What do you give?
A child has a port-wine stain and MRI calcifications. What do you do?
A child with scleroderma has Raynaud's attacks. What is true?
questions.d: It can develop into gangrene and auto-amputation

questions.question: A child has hypokalaemia, hypochloraemia, metabolic alkalosis, normal sodium, high magnesium, and no polyuria or polydipsia. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Gitelman has low magnesium and hypocalciuria; normal or high magnesium points away from Gitelman. The recall writer chose Bartter, though lack of polyuria is unusual for it.

questions.question: Which test supports a diagnosis of SLE?
A boy has features of fragile X syndrome. How is it diagnosed?
How is Werdnig-Hoffmann disease (SMA type I) diagnosed?
questions.d: Molecular genetic test for the SMN gene in blood

questions.question: A child has gross haematuria, abdominal pain and gravel in the urine. What is the cause?
A child has a systolic murmur, cardiomegaly and LVH. What is the defect?
What is the most common complication of tetralogy of Fallot?
How much does height increase per month in the second 3 months?
A child in DKA has raised ICP and coma. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Treat cerebral oedema first, then CT.

questions.question: A child has egg allergy. Which vaccine is the main concern?
questions.exp: Most egg-allergic children can have influenza and MMR vaccines safely; yellow fever vaccine contains significant egg protein. The recall writer chose influenza vaccine.

questions.question: A 5-year-old has fatigue, a firm abdominal mass, bilateral proptosis and calcification on CT. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Periorbital metastases ("raccoon eyes") and calcified mass.

questions.question: A false-positive sweat test can occur in which condition?
questions.exp: Adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, G6PD and malnutrition (marasmus) can raise sweat chloride; oedema lowers it.

questions.question: How is dermatomyositis diagnosed first?
Which factor leads to decreased 2,3-diphosphoglycerate?
A near-miss event occurred with an HIV-positive patient's sample. What is a near miss?
questions.c: An error that did not reach or harm the patient

questions.question: A child has diarrhoea and then loss of bladder control. What do you do?
A child with meningitis has Gram-positive cocci on LP. What is the treatment?
A child has feeding problems and recurrent aspiration during feeds. What is the cause?
questions.exp: H-type TEF presents later with coughing during feeds.

questions.question: A child has recurrent stereotyped bouts of vomiting with normal health between. What is the diagnosis?
A child has nightmares. When do they occur?
questions.exp: Nightmares occur in REM sleep later in the night, with recall.
questions.c: In the second half of the night, and the child remembers them

questions.question: A clumsy child has recurrent chest infections and low IgA. What is the screening test?
A child has cow's milk allergy with failure on extensively hydrolysed formula. What do you give?
A picture shows flattened intestinal villi; diarrhoea began after starting solids. What is the investigation?
A 25 kg child needs maintenance fluids. How much per day?
A child has red eyes, post-auricular lymphadenopathy and a maculopapular rash starting on the face and spreading down. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Post-auricular nodes are typical of rubella.

questions.question: A child has lesions on the toes and nails with gingival bleeding and diarrhoea. What is the management?
questions.exp: This picture of hand, foot and mouth disease (with onychomadesis) needs supportive care.

questions.question: Several children in the ICU developed severe bacterial infections and some died. What is the likely factor?
What are airborne precautions?
A child has fever, cough and respiratory distress; CXR shows bilateral diffuse infiltrates. What is the diagnosis?
A 6-year-old suddenly chokes while eating. He is conscious but cannot speak or make a sound. What is next?
questions.exp: Ineffective cough in a conscious child over 1 year: abdominal thrusts.

questions.question: A pedigree shows an affected mother with affected children of both sexes in every generation. What is the inheritance?
A pedigree shows unaffected parents, several affected sons, transmission through unaffected females and no father-to-son transmission. What is the inheritance?
A 25 kg child needs maintenance fluids. What is the daily volume?
A child previously followed objects but now no longer tracks them. What do you do?
questions.exp: Loss of visual tracking needs urgent eye review.

questions.question: A 2.5-year-old does not interact, laughs repetitively and has stereotyped movements. What is next?
questions.d: Evaluate for autism and refer for developmental assessment

questions.question: A child with fever and respiratory distress has the right cardiac border at the right midclavicular line. What does it indicate?
questions.exp: A displaced right border suggests effusion or enlargement.

questions.question: A child has oedema, hypoalbuminaemia and protein deficiency. What is the diagnosis?
A child has distended neck veins and shock. What type?
